headline: Shas leader Deri warns of high turnout in Arab sector and left strongholds
dek: The National, citing political sources, reports an 'astronomical' turnout of Arab voters is expected, rising from about 50% to 70% of the two million Arab citizens (20% of Israel's population), with the Arab parties taking 14 of 120 Knesset seats; final polls put the opposition at 56 seats and…
sources: The National (political sources); Haaretz live blog (Shas chairman Arye Deri, after voting in Jerusalem); Israel Central Elections Committee (stations open)
fault_line: Do Arab parties become kingmakers who decide Netanyahu's fate, or is Deri right that high Arab turnout is 'a danger to Judaism'?

sections.what_happened: The National, citing political sources, reports an 'astronomical' turnout of Arab voters is expected, rising from about 50% to 70% of the two million Arab citizens (20% of Israel's population), with the Arab parties taking 14 of 120 Knesset seats; final polls put the opposition at 56 seats and Netanyahu's Likud at 50, so an Eisenkot-led opposition could form a minority government with tacit Arab support or a coalition with Ra'am (Mansour Abbas). Haaretz: after voting, Shas chairman Arye Deri said turnout was expected to be particularly high in left-wing strongholds and among Arab voters, claimed tens of thousands of Israelis had arrived from abroad to vote 'to bring down the government and harm the Torah', and warned of 'a real danger to Judaism', urging turnout. The Central Elections Committee said more than 95% of polling stations were open. NO official midday turnout percentage was found in-window: the 50%-to-70% figure is an expectation from political sources, not a counted result.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct publisher families: The National + Haaretz. Deri's own quoted remarks are a primary-source claim; the Arab-turnout expectation and seat arithmetic are attributed reporting, not an official count.
sections.what_disputed: No official turnout figure yet: the Central Elections Committee statement retrieved covers stations open (>95%), not votes cast. Deri's 'tens of thousands arrived from abroad' claim is a campaign assertion with no corroboration in the retrieved copy. Final-poll seat figures differ across pollsters in prior records (opposition 52-56; Channel 14 dissent 62 for Netanyahu bloc).
sections.why_matters: The number that decides the election is not 61 yet — it is the Arab turnout: 50% to 70% could hand 14 seats the balance of power.
sections.context: Background: ELECTION-DAY MIDDAY -- Arab turnout surge expected to decide the race: The National reports 'astronomical' Arab turnout (50% to 70%); Shas leader Deri warns of high turnout in Arab sector and left strongholds

totw_analysis: Our read: The number that decides the election is not 61 yet — it is the Arab turnout: 50% to 70% could hand 14 seats the balance of power. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Do Arab parties become kingmakers who decide Netanyahu's fate, or is Deri right that high Arab turnout is 'a danger to Judaism'?
